subject.title: Feature Request: Add parseMode config for Telegram channels

question: What Telegram formatting config surface should OpenClaw support for this issue: no new parse-mode config, a narrow default-preserving plain/HTML selector, or broader MarkdownV2/raw-HTML/rich-message policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API affects user config, defaults, escaping, custom entities, rich-message behavior, and multiple send funnels, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Add Narrow Default-Preserving Selector
options.body: Expose a typed Telegram text/parse-mode config that keeps current HTML behavior by default and initially supports only modes with well-defined escaping and fallback semantics.

options.title: Keep Only richMessages
options.body: Close or defer parse-mode config and continue using `richMessages` plus internal HTML/plain fallbacks as the supported operator surface.

options.title: Design Broader Formatting Policy
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers define MarkdownV2, raw HTML/custom entities, rich messages, account inheritance, and security constraints together.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow Default-Preserving Selector
recommendation.body: Expose a typed Telegram text/parse-mode config that keeps current HTML behavior by default and initially supports only modes with well-defined escaping and fallback semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the clearest history on the HTML formatting change and recent Telegram config/docs policy, and previously framed this as a maintainer product decision.
